extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers (Scientific Review Group members) assigned to review P01 Program Project grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers on preparing written critiques, assigning preliminary scores, and applying the NIH review criteria specifically for Program Project (P01) grant applications, including evaluation of individual research projects, administrative and scientific cores, and the overall program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact/Priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an overall impact/priority score reflecting the likelihood for the project or program to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the five core review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The overall impact should reflect the interdependence of components and their potential to contribute to the overall success; it is not an average of component scores (e.g., high-merit research components may contribute little to the PPG as a whole, and conversely). Assigned reviewers should state strengths and weaknesses of the Overall Program in the template and enter a preliminary overall impact/priority score in IAR. The SRG may summarize strengths/weaknesses in a RESUME AND SUMMARY OF DISCUSSION paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? If aims are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how successful completion will change concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventative interventions that drive the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? If Early Stage Investigators or New Investigators, do they have appropriate experience and training? If established, have they demonstrated an ongoing record of accomplishments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For collaborative or multi-PD/PI projects, assess whether investigators have complementary and integrated expertise; whether leadership approach, governance and organizational structure are appropriate for the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether concepts/approaches/methodologies/instrumentation/interventions are novel to one field or novel in a broad sense, or represent a refinement, improvement, or new application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims? Are potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success presented?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For early-stage projects, evaluate whether strategy will establish feasibility and manage risky aspects. For clinical research, evaluate plans for protection of human subjects and inclusion policies (minorities, genders, children) in terms of the scientific goals and strategy. Comments about human subjects acceptability/unacceptability that affect approach should appear under Approach and be factored into the score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment in which the work will be done contribute to the probability of success?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider institutional support, equipment and physical resources, and whether the project benefits from unique features of the environment, subject populations, or collaborative arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criterion scoring procedure (individual projects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each scored review criterion for Individual Research Projects should be given a score using the nine-point rating scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion scores should be entered in the meeting IAR Web site in the NIH Commons before the review meeting (use same page as preliminary impact/priority score). Do not enter scores on the critique. Criterion scores are part of the critique but generally will not be discussed at the review meeting. Scores may be changed during the EDIT phase. In the READ phase reviewers may submit scores and critiques but may not edit them. Core criterion scores can be submitted only after critique upload into IAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique formatting and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Written critiques must follow the structured template provided (templates for Individual Research Projects, Administrative Core, Scientific Cores, and Overall Program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the downloaded template; comment on standard and additional review criteria, listing strengths and weaknesses of each in a bulleted sentence format. The goal is to provide the maximum and most pertinent information in a concise manner. Assigned reviewers must upload critiques before entering scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critiques for Individual Research Projects (required items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigned reviewers should state the strengths and weaknesses of each criterion in the appropriate section of the template, briefly summarize strengths and weaknesses in the 'Overall Impact' section, enter preliminary scores for each criterion, and enter a preliminary overall impact/priority score for the project on IAR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: assigned reviewers must upload critiques before entering scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critiques for Scientific or Administrative Cores
rubrics_metrics.description: After considering all review criteria (including FOA-specific criteria), assigned reviewers should state strengths and weaknesses of the core and rate the Core either as 'Acceptable' or 'Unacceptable' within the text of the critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support Cores are not scored numerically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Core evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application clearly describe and justify the proposed administrative core operational plan and organizational structure? Is the proposed administrative core adequate to support and encourage optimal interactions among participants?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the core leader's administrative, management, and leadership capabilities provide for internal quality control of ongoing research; management of day-to-day program activities; management of contractual agreements; fair, effective communication and cooperation among program leaders/investigators; resolution of disputes; development of scientific meetings; and allocation of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Core evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the scientific core necessary? Can it support at least two research projects? How is the core connected to the central focus of the overall program? How good are the facilities or services provided by the core (including procedures, techniques, and quality control)? Are they being used effectively?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the core leader and key personnel are well-qualified to operate the core and note any concerns about competence or commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-exempt human subjects research, evaluate the justification for involvement of human subjects and the proposed protections from research risk according to five review criteria: (1) risk to subjects, (2) adequacy of protection against risks, (3) potential benefits to the subjects and others, (4) importance of the knowledge to be gained, and (5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all criteria are adequately addressed and there are no concerns, write 'Acceptable Risks and/or Adequate Protections' (brief explanation advisable). If one or more criteria are inadequately addressed, write 'Unacceptable Risks and/or Inadequate Protections' and document issues. For clinical trials evaluate the Data and Safety Monitoring Plan (indicate 'Acceptable' or 'Unacceptable'; if absent, notify SRO). For exempt research evaluate justification for exemption, human subjects involvement and characteristics, and sources of materials; if exemption is not justified indicate 'Unacceptable' and explain. Refer to NIH Human Subjects Protection guidance and worksheet links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities and Children
rubrics_metrics.description: When clinical research is proposed, evaluate proposed plans for inclusion of minorities and members of both genders, and inclusion of children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public Law 103-43 requires inclusion of women and minorities unless clear rationale for exclusion; NIH requires inclusion of children (<21) unless scientific/ethical reasons for exclusion. Assign codes for gender (G1–G4), minority (M1–M5), and children (C1–C4) and rate recruitment targets as 'A' (acceptable) or 'U' (unacceptable). If 'U', consider this a weakness and reflect in the overall score; explain reasons for any 'U'. Comments affecting approach should appear under 'Approach'. Refer to NIH Human Subjects Protection guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate involvement of live vertebrate animals according to five points: (1) proposed use of the animals, species/strains/ages/sex/numbers; (2) justification for use and appropriateness of species and numbers; (3) adequacy of veterinary care; (4) procedures for limiting discomfort/distress/pain/injury and use of analgesic/anesthetic/tranquilizing drugs or comfortable restraining devices; (5) methods of euthanasia and reason if not consistent with AVMA Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the Vertebrate Animals section is 'Acceptable' or 'Unacceptable' and refer to the VAS checklist for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether adequate protection is proposed and document any concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing a Resubmission (amended) application, evaluate the application as now presented, taking into consideration responses to comments from the previous scientific review group and changes made to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess adequacy of responses and whether revisions address previous concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing a Renewal (competing continuation) application, consider the progress made in the last funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate accomplishments to date and whether proposed renewal is justified by prior progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing a Revision (competing supplement) application, consider the appropriateness of the proposed expansion of the scope of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Revision relates to a line of investigation previously not recommended for approval, consider whether responses to prior comments are adequate and whether substantial changes are clearly evident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period Support (additional review consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider whether the budget and the requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not give a separate score for this item; comment as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess the information provided about Select Agent(s) to be used in the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess: which select agents will be used; the registration status of all entities where select agents will be used; procedures to monitor possession, use and transfer; and plans for appropriate biosafety, biocontainment, and security. Refer to NIH select agent policy link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the project presents special opportunities for furthering research through the use of unusual talent, resources, populations, or environmental conditions that exist in other countries and either are not readily available in the U.S. or augment existing U.S. resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on whether foreign aspects provide unique added value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans (Data sharing, Model organisms, GWAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether resource sharing plans, or the rationale for not sharing, are reasonable: (1) Data Sharing Plan (expected for applications requesting >$500,000 direct costs unless FOA specifies otherwise); (2) Sharing Model Organisms (expected in all applications where development of model organisms is anticipated); (3) GWAS data submission plan (expected for GWAS proposals regardless of cost).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the reasonableness of the plan or rationale for not sharing and cite applicable NIH policy links.
